close_reason: Delivered in PR #282 (audited 2026-09-06: always-multicall highest epoch, periodic revalidation, client-side epoch fence; 7 tests; one CI job red on unrelated repo_transact_test flake)
description: Rediscovery only triggers on DOWN/ping failure; a partitioned old leader that stays alive retains its links indefinitely. Pre-existing liveness question surfaced in bedrock-q67.4 audit. Consider periodic leader re-verification or coordinator-side epoch fencing on link traffic.

comments.text: Draft PR: https://github.com/bedrock-kv/bedrock/pull/282 — Link now re-polls the whole coordinator set on a jittered 5s interval (highest epoch wins) instead of trusting the leader it is pinned to, and fences {:tsl_updated, _} pushes against a wiring_epoch high-water mark. Cold audit PASS-WITH-NOTES; all three notes addressed.

Status note (2026-09-14): this ticket is closed but its fix, PR #282, is still OPEN/unmerged and origin/develop (153a2b62) has no Link re-polling. Reproduced live in the 3-node harness during bedrock-w10 verification: after two elections without process death (leadership w2 -> w3 -> w1, see bedrock-5yi), every node's Link stayed pinned to w2's alive-but-follower coordinator with the epoch-2 TSL; clients got :unavailable indefinitely, and Foreman.advertise_running_worker registered new log workers via Raft.add_transaction on that follower (result ignored), so the epoch-4 leader's service directory never learned the epoch-3 log and its recovery stalled on :unable_to_meet_log_quorum forever.

title: Link discovery: partitioned-but-alive old coordinator leader is never abandoned
